I have spent more time on this waiver wire than on any in years, and the injury list is the reason. De’Von Achane tore his ACL, Breece Hall is week to week with a quad injury and Travis Etienne will miss time with a hamstring, so 3 backfields opened up in a single weekend.

Allen is the top claim on this wire even though Hall is not out for the season. Hall avoided a serious injury, and he could be back in 2 weeks or it could take 4, but for as long as he is out Allen is the lead back in New York. He has been Hall’s backup for years, he has the size to handle a 3 down workload, he catches the ball, and I expect him to be a top 24 back in Week 4.
The Jets are not a good offense, but there are tiers to bad. The betting markets have them as a bottom 10 offense, while Miami projects as the worst offense in the league by a wide margin. That gap is why Allen goes ahead of Ollie Gordon on my list, even though Gordon’s opening lasts the whole season.

This is where most leagues will spend their budget, and Gordon should be rostered everywhere. When Achane went down against Kansas City, Gordon handled a 3 down workload with the receiving work included. The rushing efficiency was poor, but he was running behind the Miami line in an offense with nothing else working, so I do not put that on him.
The problem is the backfield will not stay his alone. Jaylen Wright missed Week 3 with a stinger, the early reporting has him joining Gordon in Week 4, and everything out of Miami points to a committee. I have a real bid in on Gordon myself, and I am ready to bench him in Week 4 until I see the split. If it is a true committee in the worst offense in the league, he could be a drop in 2 or 3 weeks, but a possible starting running back is worth the roster spot until we know.

I had Kamara as a deeper league handcuff behind Etienne in the Week 3 email, and now Etienne is out with a hamstring. He will not play in Week 4, and I would not be surprised if he misses the next month, with the Saints’ Week 8 bye giving him extra time before a possible Week 9 return.
Kamara does not have the legs he used to, and he will split the work with Kendre Miller and maybe a third back. What keeps him interesting in full PPR is the receiving work in an offense that looks good, with Tyler Shough dropping back as often as he does. Think a handful of short catches rather than a breakout, which makes him a flex play in a 12 team league if you are thin at running back. He is a committee back with a 3 or 4 week window, which is why he sits behind Allen, the feature back, and Gordon, whose opening lasts all season.

Sadiq was the Jets’ first round pick, a freak athlete at tight end who missed a good chunk of camp with a sports hernia, so I expected a slow start. Then, with Omar Cooper Jr. already on injured reserve, Adonai Mitchell was ruled out against Detroit with a finger injury, the Jets were down a tight end as well, and Sadiq drew the traditional tight end usage and made the big plays.
He should be rostered in every league, and if Kyle Pitts is your second tight end, I would cut Pitts for him. Temper it a little: Detroit was close to a perfect matchup and Adonai Mitchell could be back in Week 4, so he is not a set and forget starter yet. The upside is why you add him now.

DEEPER LEAGUES
Kendre Miller  RB · NO
Week 3 vs LV: 4 carries · 14 rushing yards · 3 targets · 3.9 PPR
The other half of the New Orleans split while Etienne is out. Kamara is the better full PPR bet because of the receiving work, but Miller gets carries in an offense that moves the ball, and a third back may take a share too.
Jaylen Wright  RB · MIA
Week 3: did not play
The other half of what should be a Miami committee once he is back from the stinger. Neither back is that talented in the worst offense in the league, but one of them could be the starter for the rest of the season, so roster Gordon first and Wright in deeper leagues.
Keaton Mitchell  RB · LAC
Week 3 at BUF: 8 carries · 52 rushing yards · 3 targets · 13.7 PPR
Looked better than Omarion Hampton in Week 3 and gave the Chargers the explosive plays they have been missing, so he belongs on your watch list. He is a handcuff in the Tyler Allgeier mold, not startable unless Hampton gets hurt, and the Chargers project as a bottom 5 offense the rest of the way with a brutal schedule ahead.
DON’T CHASE
Bo Nix  QB · DEN
Week 3 vs LAR: 186 passing yards · 2 passing TDs · 7 rushing yards · 24.1 PPR
Viable in deeper formats, but not the pickup for Week 4. He has not reached 10 rushing yards in a game all season, he struggled through the first 2 weeks before the good game against the Rams, and he has to play at San Francisco.
Oronde Gadsden  TE · LAC
Week 3 at BUF: 3 targets · 0 receptions · 0 yards · 0.0 PPR
I had him as a stash in the Week 3 email, and he gave you a zero against Buffalo. It is safe to send him back to the waiver wire.
QUARTERBACK STREAMERS
Jared Goff  QB · DET
Week 3 vs NYJ: 269 passing yards · 2 passing TDs · 6 rushing yards · 19.4 PPR
The best streamer if he is somehow available in your league. Detroit plays at Carolina in a game with one of the highest totals on the slate, and with the Lions’ defense struggling, the offense has to keep throwing.
Bryce Young  QB · CAR
Week 3 at CLE: 291 passing yards · 1 passing TD · 0 rushing yards · 13.6 PPR
The other side of the same game. He struggled against Cleveland and still threw it 48 times, and a matchup with that Detroit defense in a high scoring game makes him a viable stream.
Kyler Murray  QB · MIN
Week 3 at TB: 168 passing yards · 1 passing TD · 17 rushing yards · 10.4 PPR
Viable if Justin Jefferson is back, and the imaging on his sprained ankle showed no long term damage, which gives him a chance to play in Week 4. The Week 3 line at Tampa Bay came with Jefferson off the field for most of the game, and Minnesota projects well at home against Miami. He is the streamer I would roll with in a deeper league.
DEFENSES TO STREAM
My pick: Ravens vs Titans
Tennessee has to travel to Baltimore and projects as one of the 2 lowest scoring offenses on the slate, ahead of only Miami. It is the best defense you can probably still get, and it is the claim I would make.
Also in play
Packers at Buccaneers · Steelers at Browns
How I pick them
I stream defenses off the betting markets: the biggest spread and the lowest projected total for the other offense. Minnesota against Miami and Seattle against the Chargers are the best plays in Week 4, but both are probably rostered, and if you took the Vikings on the Week 3 pick, you are already set.
